Hi Alina — great context, thanks. I put together a short runbook covering: model shortlist, context strategies (prefixing + retrieval vs chunked context), rough token/day estimates, and immediate asks for engineering. Attaching the MAP and token sample sheet.

Topline (short):
- Model shortlist: 1) rwd-3.7b-enc (low-latency, good for summarization), 2) rwd-7b-q4_0 (balanced cost/quality), 3) open-llama-13b-qlora (for long-history synthesis when higher quality needed).
- Context approach: hybrid retrieval-first (512 token prompt + retrieved snippets up to 6k tokens) and progressive KV caching for patient sessions to reduce repeat costs. For very long histories (>12k tokens), use chunked retrieval + stitching with a short final pass.
- Token sizing (first pass): steady 120k gen tokens/day, prompt tokens estimated 60k/day (retrieval snippets), peak 1.2M gen tokens/day with prompt tokens up to 600k/day during weekly reporting.

Immediate asks:
1) Can your eng team share sample note volumes per clinician (daily avg) and typical session length?
2) Any regulatory requirement for on-prem or VPC-only?
3) Are there hard latency p95 targets for batch vs interactive flows?

I've copied Marissa (CS lead) and Rishi (solutions/infra) to scope Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs. I will schedule a 30m design call — link: https://cal.com/priyom/30m?ref=noblecare

Attachments: NobleCare-MAP-v1.xlsx, noblecare_token_samples.csv
